messages.t:
I'm Detective Theo Marsh. I have parts of the investigation file. What I don't have is the complete wedding ledger. You do.

I've been going back through the evidence the original investigation used against Jasmine.

There's something bothering me about it.

The case against her is built around what she did before Margery died.

I'm interested in what happened after Margery left the reception.

Let's start with the evidence I can recover.

I went back through the CCTV report.

Most of the reception was covered, but there was a gap in the camera coverage. The report places the blind spot around Tables 46 through 50.

That's important, but it doesn't tell us who was there.

Check that section of the wedding ledger for me.

That's still too many people.

I went back to the physical evidence.

There's a handwritten mark on one of the items recovered during the investigation. It's damaged, but I can make out what might be a first initial.

T, H, J, or I.

I'm not confident enough to say which one it is.

See what that does to the group.

I also had the lab re-check something recovered from the reception.

They identified chicken gravy.

It may give us another way to narrow the same group.

Check the meal field.
Check the evidence against the ledger again. Tell me what you find.
Check the evidence against the ledger again. Tell me what you find.
Check the evidence against the ledger again. Tell me what you find.

Now we're starting to see a pattern.

I found another detail in the evidence file.

One of the guest badges recovered from the relevant area was pink. The reception records distinguish between the bride's side and the groom's side.

Check which of the remaining records belong to the bride's side.

That's a much smaller group.

I went back through the final seating records because there's something unusual about the last revision.

The seating plan was updated after the RSVP deadline. The revision included people from the late-confirmation list.

Check the remaining records against the late-confirmation initials: E or L.

Eleven.

I found another piece of the evidence that may help.

An unidentified wedding gift was recorded in the inventory. We never established who sent it, but the inventory gives us an approximate value.

It falls somewhere between $50 and $150.

Check that value range against the eleven remaining records.

Only two people still fit everything we've found.

I went back to the evidence recovered from the reception.

There's a torn seating marker. Most of it is missing, but one detail is still readable:

Table 49.

I don't have the seat number.

Check the two remaining records against Table 49. Who's left?
Check the evidence against the ledger again. Tell me what you find.

Iris Smith. Table 49, Seat 8.

That's our person.

But a name isn't a murder.

I want to know who Iris was, what her relationship with Margery was, and what brought her into this investigation.

That's where your side of the investigation becomes important.
The Legal Team has released its background material on Iris. Read it, then come back and tell me what you learned.

docs.title: WHO IS IRIS?
docs.body:
Iris Smith works in event design and logistics. She was professionally involved in the Alder Hollow wedding and had worked with Margery on previous events.

Margery relied on Iris when event-design or production problems needed solving. Iris was not simply a wedding guest.

progress.task: Use the Legal Team to investigate who Iris was, how she worked with Margery, and what changed between them.
